Anza Renewables reported a $0.15/W to $0.20/W price premium for PV modules dc dc assembled in the United States with U.S.-made cells relative to imported PV modules—relatively consistent with the price differences shown in Figure 12 (Anza Renewables 2025). 2.3.5 Upstream Inputs for Crystalline-Silicon Modules Table 1 reports cost estimates for the primary module assembly materials and equipment in the United States and Asia, as well as estimated use of U.S. suppliers in 2024. The information is from NLR interviews of U.S. module assembly firms and materials and equipment suppliers. • Cells: Discussed in Section 2.4. • Tabbing and busbar ribbons: Domestic availability of this material in 2024 is estimated at around 5%, and only one module vendor has been confirmed to use domestically produced metal ribbons. • Encapsulant: Interview data suggest more domestic encapsulant use in 2024 than use of any other balance-of-module material. One U.S. module assembly firm estimated that total planned domestic encapsulant capacity could ramp to around 25 GW -equivalent by dc 2027. Encapsulant extrusions are also easier to set up than glass lines (beginning with the fact glass melts at a much higher temperature) and requires much less capital. • Backsheets: For use in monofacial modules, there was significant U.S. backsheet production in 2024. Three U.S. module assembly firms were confirmed to use domestic backsheets in 2024. The combined 2024 capacity of these firms is greater than 7 GW , dc with the largest of the three also selling utility-size modules. Residential modules made in the United States with domestic backsheets are estimated at around 50% of the market. • Glass: Discussed in Section 2.8. • Frames: With enough demand pull, switching metal extrusions to the profile for PV module frames is straightforward, and at least 10 operations could do so within the United States. However, only two U.S. module assembly firms with total combined production up to 2.7 GW in 2024 were known to use domestic frame materials. PV dc frames represented a very small share of sales from U.S. aluminum extrusion companies in 2024, which we believe was due to competition from low-cost imports and the competing uses for aluminum extrusions including construction, automotive, electronics, and ubiquitous consumer products.
